questions.question: In a row of 21 students, when Murali was shifted by four places towards the right, he became 12th from the left end. What was his earlier position from the right end of the row?
questions.solution:
As per the given information,

In a row of 21 students, when Murali was shifted by four places towards the right, he became 12th from the left end.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/09d34aade066dfec72f8dfadb76614380234b90bd1645aef8ae8ba3e50f8c1c7.png] 

Now,

**The new position of Murali from the left is 12th thus before shifting by four places towards the right the position of Murali was 8th from the left.**

**So, the earlier position of Murali = 8th**

Now,

**Total students = Earlier position of Murali from left + Earlier position of Murali from right - 1**

⇒ 21 = 8 + Earlier position of Murali from right - 1

⇒ 21 = 7 + Earlier position of Murali from right

⇒ Earlier position of Murali from right = 21 - 7

⇒ Earlier position of Murali from right = 14

Thus, Murali's earlier position from the right end of the row is '14th'.

Hence, the correct answer is "14th".

questions.question: Which of the following tissues is found below the skin and between the internal organs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Option 4.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Adipose tissue** which is known as** body fat**, is found below the skin and between the internal organs.
 
• It is a** connective tissue** that extends throughout your body. 
 
• It is found under the skin **(subcutaneous fat)**, between internal organs** (visceral fat)**, and even in the inner cavities of bones** (bone marrow adipose tissue)** and in** breast tissue**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Adipose tissue consists of lipid-rich cells called **adipocytes.**
 
• The adipocytes are storage reservoirs that store fat globules in a structural network of fibers. 
 
• Apart from storage, it also serves as a cushion and insulator to protect our bodies.
 
• **Types of Adipocyte-**__There are three types of Adipocytes.

 
 

 **TYPE OF ADIPOCYTES**
 **DESCRIPTION**
 
 

 **White Adipocyte**
 
 __
 
• Filled with a single, large lipid droplet and some cellular organelles.
 
 
 
 

 **Brown Adipocyte**
 
 
 
• Filled with multiple lipid droplets and has a large number of mitochondria that help it generate heat.
 
• Commonly occurs in newborn organisms and starts to decrease as the organism ages.
 
 
 
 

 **Beige Adipocyte**
 
 
 
• Found scattered between the white adipocytes 
 
 
 
 

**Function of Adipose tissue-**__

 
 

 TYPE OF ADIPOCYTES
 **Function**
 
 

 White Adipocyte
 
 __
 
• Insulator
 
• Energy reservoir at the time of starvation and exertion
 
• Releases a number of hormones, such as leptin, resistin, and adiponectin, that play various roles in metabolism
 
 
 
 

 Brown Adipocyte
 
 
 
• Generate heat and consume energy
 
• In animals that hibernate, brown adipose tissue persists even in adolescence because these tissues help in their survival at the time of hibernation.
 
 
 
 

 Beige Adipocyte
 
 
 
• The ability to generate heat under conditions, such as exposure to cold or stimulation of the adrenergic receptors. They are also known as Brite adipocytes.

questions.question: After the 42nd Amendment, education is placed under which Constitutional list?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Concurrent List**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act** of the Constitution of India, enacted in **1976**, transferred the subject of **education** from the **State List** to the **Concurrent List**. This means that both the **Central Government** and the **State Governments** can now legislate on matters related to education.
 
• The **Concurrent List** is a list of subjects defined in the **Seventh Schedule** of the Indian Constitution on which both the **Parliament** and the **State Legislatures** are competent to make laws.
 
• Prior to the 42nd Amendment, education was solely under the **State List**, allowing only state governments to regulate and legislate on educational policies and practices.
 
• The amendment aimed to bring uniformity in education across the country and enable the Central Government to play a more significant role in framing educational policies and programs.
 
• The change was considered essential to address the growing importance of education in **nation-building** and improving literacy rates across India.
 
• The **Concurrent List** now allows the Central Government to implement national-level policies like the **Right to Education Act (RTE), 2009**, while states retain the power to adapt and implement these policies as per regional requirements.
 
• **Hence, education was placed in the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment Act.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** divides the legislative powers between the Union and the States into three lists: the **Union List**, the **State List**, and the **Concurrent List**.
 
• The **Union List** contains subjects of national importance, such as **defense, foreign affairs, and atomic energy**, on which only the Parliament can legislate.
 
• The **State List** includes subjects of regional and local importance, such as **police, public health, and agriculture**, on which only the State Legislatures can legislate.
 
• The **Concurrent List** includes subjects on which both the Parliament and State Legislatures can legislate. Examples include **education, marriage, and adoption**. However, in case of a conflict, the law made by the Parliament prevails.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976:**
 
 
• The **42nd Amendment** is also known as the **“Mini-Constitution”** due to the extensive changes it made to the Indian Constitution.
 
• It introduced several changes, including the addition of the words **“Socialist”** and **“Secular”** to the Preamble and the establishment of the **Fundamental Duties** under **Article 51A**.
 
• The amendment also aimed to strengthen the power of the Central Government and brought changes to the Seventh Schedule, including transferring education to the **Concurrent List**.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• Significant national-level education policies like the **National Education Policy (NEP)** and initiatives like **Skill India** have been possible due to education being on the Concurrent List.
 
• The **Right to Education Act (RTE), 2009**, which guarantees free and compulsory education to children aged 6 to 14, is a critical example of the Central Government’s role in education after the amendment.
 
• States retain flexibility in implementing these policies to address regional and local needs, ensuring a balance of power between the Union and the States.

State of Kerala** case (1973) is one of the most significant judgments in Indian constitutional history. • The Supreme Court laid down the **"Basic Structure Doctrine"**, which restricts the power of the Parliament to amend the Constitution in a way that alters its fundamental structure. • According to the judgment, while the Parliament has the authority under **Article 368** of the Indian Constitution to amend any part of the Constitution, it cannot alter or destroy its basic structure or essential features. • The basic structure includes principles such as the supremacy of the Constitution, separation of powers, fundamental rights, and the rule of law. • This doctrine ensures that the core principles of the Indian Constitution remain preserved, even as the Constitution evolves through amendments.
